# Static Analysis Approaches

## Analysis Techniques

### AST-Based (pyan3)

Pyan3 walks the Python AST to extract bindings (defining/assigning names) and
names in `ast.Load` context [15]. The analyzer uses `ast` and `symtable` modules
[15]. Supports nested attribute access (`self.a.b`), inherited attribute lookup
across base classes, static `super()` resolution respecting MRO, and assignment
tracking with lexical scoping [15].

Limitations: described by its own maintainers as "rather superficial" [15].
Does not track inter-procedural flow of functions, which causes low recall [9].

### Inter-Procedural Fixpoint (PyCG)

PyCG computes all assignment relations between program identifiers of functions,
variables, classes, and modules through an inter-procedural analysis [1]. It
operates on an intermediate representation and uses context-insensitive fixpoint
iteration [1].

**Performance on micro-benchmarks [1]:**
- Precision: ~99.2%
- Recall: ~69.9%
- Sound call graphs: 103/112 benchmarks
- Complete call graphs: 111/112 benchmarks
- Average speed: 0.38 seconds per 1,000 LoC

**Scalability failures [2]:**
- Fails on programs >2,000 LoC in whole-program mode
- 4 of 6 real-world apps exceeded 24-hour timeout
- 1 recursion error, 1 out-of-memory at 8 GB

PyCG is 2x slower than Pyan and uses 2.8x more memory than Depends [1].

### Flow-Sensitive Type Graphs (JARVIS)

JARVIS maintains a type graph per function for flow-sensitive intra-procedural
analysis [2]. Generates call graphs on-the-fly without global fixpoint iterations
[2]. Strong updates of types reduce false positives [2].

**Improvement over PyCG [2]:**

| Metric | Improvement |
|--------|------------|
| Speed (whole-program CGC) | ≥67% faster |
| Precision | 84% higher |
| Recall | ≥20% higher |
| Avg time (app-centered) | 8.16 seconds |
| Avg memory (app-centered) | 227 MB |

JARVIS extends PyCG's micro-benchmark from 112 to 135 programs, adding
categories for context managers and control flow [2].

### Comparison of Static Tools

| Tool | Precision | Recall | Sound | Scalable |
|------|-----------|--------|-------|----------|
| PyCG [1] | ~99.2% | ~69.9% | 103/112 | No (>2k LoC fails) |
| JARVIS [2] | Higher by 84% | Higher by ≥20% | Improved | Yes (tested on Airflow) |
| Pyan [9] | Average | Low | No | Yes (superficial) |
| Depends [9] | 98.7% | 14.4% | No | Yes |

Depends achieves near-perfect precision but misses 85% of calls [9]. This
illustrates the fundamental trade-off: sound analysis (catching all calls)
requires over-approximation that introduces false positives.

### LLM-Based and Hybrid Approaches

Static analysis tools significantly outperform LLMs in call graph generation [3].
However, InferCG combines static analysis with LLM-based semantic reasoning to
address cases where traditional methods fail on dynamic features [4].

## Python Features and Tool Coverage

| Feature | PyCG | JARVIS | Pyan3 |
|---------|------|--------|-------|
| Higher-order functions | Yes [1] | Yes [2] | Partial [15] |
| Complex inheritance | Yes [1] | Yes [2] | Yes (MRO) [15] |
| Nested definitions | Yes [1] | Yes [2] | Yes [15] |
| Context managers | No [2] | Yes [2] | Yes [15] |
| Built-in types | No [2] | Yes [2] | N/A |
| Control flow | Partial [2] | Yes [2] | N/A |
| Walrus operator | N/A | N/A | Yes [15] |
| Match statements | N/A | N/A | Yes [15] |
| Async/await | N/A | N/A | Yes [15] |
| Module-level imports | Yes [14] | Yes [2] | Yes (--module-level) [15] |

## Gaps and Limitations

- PyCG's micro-benchmark precision (99.2%) may not reflect real-world accuracy
  given its complete failure on 4 of 6 macro-benchmark apps [2].
- JARVIS exists only as a research artifact, not a maintained tool [17].
- No tool handles all Python dynamic features — see
  [accuracy-limitations.md](accuracy-limitations.md) for details.
- The 2025 Springer study confirms that even LLMs cannot replace static tools
  for call graph generation [3], but static tools still miss 30%+ of calls [1].
